Compare Two Local GHO Data Snapshots

Source: R/compare_snapshots.R
compare_snapshots.Rd

Matches observations by their full semantic key and reports additions, removals, value changes and metadata changes. Everything runs offline.

Usage 

compare_snapshots(old, new, fields = NULL, tolerance = 0)

Arguments

old, new

Objects returned by data_snapshot(), or local RDS paths containing such objects. Plain data frames and snapshot() cache files do not carry the required comparison contract.

fields

Optional character vector of non-key fields to compare. Default NULL compares the union of all non-key data columns, including labels, notes, service record IDs and provider-reported timestamps. Snapshot and retrieval times are context, not observation changes.

tolerance

A single non-negative, finite absolute numeric tolerance. Default 0 compares numbers exactly. It applies to numeric fields, not dates, times, character strings or matching keys. Original values remain unrounded. A display string can still change when numbers are within tolerance; use fields explicitly to compare numeric fields alone.

Value

A list, classed dsir_snapshot_comparison, containing:

summary

A one-row tibble with old/new snapshot and retrieval times, source, backend, indicator, query scope, observation counts, n_added, n_removed, n_modified, n_unchanged, n_value_modified, n_metadata_only, n_metadata_modified, selected fields and tolerance.

added,removed

Complete new-only and old-only observation rows.

modified

Key columns, primary old_value and new_value, absolute/relative changes, change flags, change_type, a changed_fields list-column, and old / new data-frame columns containing complete old/new tables aligned with the modified rows. For example, modified$old[1, ] is the first original old row.

unchanged

Complete new rows whose selected fields are unchanged.

schema_changes

Non-key fields added, removed or changed in type, independent of whether their values changed.

key,fields,value_fields

The identity and selected comparison fields.

Details

Comparison stops when source, backend, indicator, layout, origin, query scope, key columns or value definitions differ. Changes in the available unit or measure-family codes also stop comparison: these can change the meaning of a quantity. Equal scope is necessary, not sufficient proof of scientific comparability. Imported data and local subsets require an explicit, honest scope declaration when making their snapshots.

Matching ignores row order, column order and row names. Missing values match missing values. An entirely missing logical column from JSON can be compared with a later typed column; integer and double numbers are compatible. Other incompatible field types cause an actionable error. Missing optional metadata columns are compared as missing values, with their schema differences reported separately. List-column note order is retained; NULL, an empty vector and a scalar NA denote an absent note.

A matched observation is modified when at least one selected field changes. value_changed concerns selected value_fields; other selected fields determine metadata_changed. A modification with no selected value change is labelled "metadata_only". Selecting fields restricts every change classification; unselected differences are not counted.

absolute_change is the signed difference new_value - old_value in the primary numeric field's units. relative_change is that difference divided by the old value, a fraction rather than a percentage. It is NA for zero/missing old values, missing new values or non-finite calculations. These convenience columns concern the primary value even when another field triggered the modification.

This establishes differences between two saved extracts. It does not establish their exact change date, revision reason or official WHO publication status. Counts of added, removed and value-modified rows can inform whether to review existing outputs; the caller decides whether those rows or changed labels/notes affect a particular report.

See also

data_snapshot(), gho_last_updated().

Examples 

# See data_snapshot() for a complete offline example.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
result <- compare_snapshots("snapshots/gho_old.rds",
                            "snapshots/gho_new.rds")
result$summary
result$modified
# For a report using numeric values and bounds only:
compare_snapshots("snapshots/gho_old.rds", "snapshots/gho_new.rds",
                  fields = c("NumericValue", "Low", "High"))
} # }
